headline: A Complete Open-Source System for AI Coding Agents
lede: When Affaan Mustafa won the Anthropic x Forum Ventures hackathon last September — building an AI customer-discovery tool in eight hours — he walked away with $15,000 in API credits and a refined sense of how to extract consistent performance from Claude Code, Anthropic's agentic coding assistant. Four months later, he open-sourced the techniques. The result, *everything-claude-code*, now carries more than 175,000 GitHub stars and has become the most widely circulated third-party configuration system for AI coding agents.
body:
**Claude Code** is Anthropic's command-line coding agent: it reads codebases, edits files, runs shell commands, and handles git operations, guided by large-language-model reasoning and a *hooks* architecture that fires shell scripts on lifecycle events. Out of the box it works, but it ships without opinions about workflow structure, cost management, or security. That is the gap *everything-claude-code* fills.

The repository ships as a Claude Code plugin — a directory of configuration files the tool reads on startup. As of its second major version, it bundles 48 specialized *subagents* (markdown instruction files that tell the model when to delegate to a focused helper), 182 *skills* (reusable workflow definitions spanning test-driven development, database patterns, and cost-aware pipeline routing), and 68 *slash-command* shims that map short mnemonics like /plan and /tdd to those workflows. An always-on rules layer enforces language-specific conventions for twelve ecosystems — TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Kotlin, Swift, and others. The system also supports competing AI coding environments including Cursor, Codex CLI, and OpenCode.

The most distinctive component is *AgentShield*, a companion package distributed separately on npm that scans AI agent configurations for security vulnerabilities. Its rule set — 102 checks across five categories covering secrets exposure, permission scope, hook safety, *Model Context Protocol* (MCP) server configuration, and instruction-injection risks — runs against the configuration files that AI coding agents read on startup. The ECC changelog credits AgentShield with 1,282 individual tests. A premium tier runs a three-agent adversarial pipeline in which one Claude Opus instance attacks a configuration, another defends it, and a third audits the exchange — a *red-team/blue-team* methodology more common in enterprise penetration testing than in open-source developer tooling.

One claim warrants scrutiny. The "60% cost reduction" advertised in the post refers not to a measured benchmark but to a configuration recommendation in the README: switching Claude Code's default model from Claude Opus to Claude Sonnet, which Anthropic prices at roughly one-fifth the cost per token. Mustafa's assertion that Sonnet handles roughly 80% of coding tasks adequately is plausible, but characterizing the resulting savings as "documented" implies a controlled experiment that does not exist in the public record.

The repository's trajectory — from nine agents at launch in January 2026 to its present scale in under four months — tracks a broader shift in how developers relate to AI coding tools. The configurable layer atop the model is becoming its own engineering discipline: how to structure delegation, manage context across sessions, enforce conventions automatically, and keep token costs predictable. Mustafa's project is among the first to treat that layer as a first-class artifact worth sharing, versioning, and auditing for safety.

concepts.definition: Anthropic's agentic command-line coding assistant. It reads codebases, edits files, runs shell commands, and handles git operations under natural-language direction, using a large language model as its core reasoning engine.

Shell scripts registered to fire automatically on Claude Code lifecycle events — file edits, session starts, shell commands, or session end. They let developers inject custom behavior (secret scanning, memory persistence, dangerous-flag blocking) without changing the model's instructions directly.

In Claude Code, a markdown file that describes a specialized AI assistant with a narrowly defined role — for example, a security reviewer or build-error resolver. The primary agent can delegate subtasks to a subagent, which runs with its own context and toolset.

Reusable workflow definition files in the everything-claude-code system. Each skill encodes a domain-specific procedure — how to run a security review, structure a TDD cycle, or route LLM calls by cost — that agents can invoke by name rather than rediscovering each time.

A security scanner for AI agent configurations, distributed as a standalone npm package (ecc-agentshield). It checks CLAUDE.md files, MCP server configurations, and hooks for vulnerabilities including secrets exposure, over-broad permissions, and prompt-injection risks.

An open protocol developed by Anthropic that standardizes how AI models connect to external tools, APIs, and data sources. MCP servers expose capabilities — file access, web search, database queries — that a Claude Code session can invoke during a task.

An adversarial security testing methodology in which one group (the red team) attempts to breach a system while another (the blue team) defends it. Borrowed from military exercises, the approach is standard in enterprise cybersecurity. AgentShield's premium mode runs separate AI instances in each role, with a third acting as auditor.

A short text trigger prefixed with a forward slash — such as /plan or /tdd — that maps to a longer skill or workflow in Claude Code. The everything-claude-code project ships 68 such shims as convenience aliases for its most-used procedures.

repos.summary: A comprehensive Claude Code plugin system providing 48 specialized subagents, 182 workflow skills, 68 slash-command shims, and security scanning via AgentShield. Built by Affaan Mustafa from techniques developed during the Anthropic x Forum Ventures hackathon and refined over months of daily use building production products. Supports twelve language ecosystems and integrates with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, and OpenCode.

A standalone security scanner for AI agent configurations, extracting the AgentShield component of everything-claude-code into its own project. Distributed as the ecc-agentshield npm package, it runs 102 rules across five vulnerability categories against CLAUDE.md files, hooks, and MCP server configurations. Its advanced mode deploys three separate Claude Opus instances in a red-team/blue-team/auditor adversarial pipeline.

fact_check: The component counts in the post — 27 agents, 64 skills, 33 commands — are outdated; the current v2.0.0 release lists 48 agents, 182 skills, and 68 slash-command shims. The "60% documented cost reduction" is not a benchmarked result but the author's own estimate for switching the default model from Claude Opus to Claude Sonnet, presented in the README as a configuration table, not a measured experiment. The "Anthropic hackathon winner" framing is accurate — Mustafa won the Anthropic x Forum Ventures hackathon (New York, September 2025) — but the winning project was zenith.chat, an AI customer-discovery platform built in eight hours; the ECC repository itself was open-sourced four months later.
